## Implementation examples and visual chapters

- Six alternating copy-and-visual chapters cover: shared Locale Insight architecture with distinct Land/Location/Living product truth; Initial HTML → Visible page → Hydrated state parity; prominent/calm navigation; Web/PDF/deck/social semantic parity; parcel/neighbourhood incompatibility; and a static rejected-motion recovery.
- Every chapter is a conceptual design-system teaching fixture, not product or city evidence. The alternating presentation is a non-normative artifact decision.
- Initial HTML, visible page, and hydrated state preserve the same claim, source, time basis, limitation, and action authority.
- Navigation uses direct named destinations, a disclosure button with stable focus recovery, and separate current-page/current-location states. The header may move between visually prominent and calm states, but every semantic link/button remains direct and at least 44 × 44 CSS pixels; no wake-first or coordinate-forwarding layer is permitted.
- Icons remain rounded outline at FILL 0 in every state.
- Motion roles are limited to approach.soft, approach.inline-start, approach.inline-end, media.arrival, and stagger.child. Constants are 760ms opacity, 920ms transform, 900ms media, 32px block distance, 36px logical-inline distance, .985 starting scale, 150ms stagger capped at 450ms, .14 observer threshold, 0px 0px -12% 0px root margin, and a 2400ms safety audit.
- Hero/LCP media, H1, first answer, primary proof, primary action, task-critical state, status, focus targets, deep-link targets, closed disclosures, and hidden panels are excluded from hidden entrances. Motion is once-only and fail-open; reduced motion, missing observer support, or no JavaScript receives visible final meaning.
- The finite CTA cue moves a pointer-inert 28% highlight band from -120% to 120% once in 540ms with cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); it does not loop, move layout, or change content opacity.
- Web, PDF, deck, and social outputs preserve semantic meaning rather than pixel sameness.
- Incompatibility is a valid result when schema, release, unit, or grain differs.
- The complete Color Atlas and Color Set color-srgb-05 are unchanged; this UI revision does not mint a new Color Set.
- Open-menu locale changes preserve the currently focused control, deep links use one sticky-header offset, and standalone browser-tab identity embeds the approved favicon for offline use.

## Evidence and capability boundaries

- All teaching cases on this page are conceptual unless a named product-specific adaptation says otherwise.
- This reference is not evidence about a city, place, product, audience, or outcome.
- It is not a Full Living Reference.
- Cross-product or cross-city comparison requires a compatible schema and release, with unit and grain reconciled; otherwise the incompatibility must remain visible.
- CityMETER, CityWiki, CityChat, ijji, municipality, retail, F&B, land-valuation, flood, and other named-product or domain assumptions must not be generalized to the shared Landometer layer.
- The Complete Color Atlas is a design reference. A product analysis must bind its own compatible data release and evidence before using analytical scales.
- The page does not save, share, invite, publish, track, or mutate a remote governed object.

## Machine-use rules

- Preserve object ID, version, scope, boundary, time, source, missingness, confidence, limitation, allowed use, visibility, and authoritative state.
- Never upgrade partial to complete, modelled to observed, planned to available, sent to received, a handoff to a network effect, or discovery to evidence.
- Readability does not grant permission to act.
- Do not infer an action endpoint from a human-facing link or control.
- Do not infer that the Design System release pre-certifies a downstream artifact or product claim.

This project-path llms.txt is a navigation aid only. It is not a ranking signal, crawler directive, access-control rule, conformance certificate, or permission for an agent to act.
